findings.prompt_en: Tara says 10 houses need 40 sticks because each house adds 4. Check her.
findings.key: She forgot the first house needs 5 (one extra stick): 4 × 10 + 1 = 41 (acceptable: '41', 'wrong')
findings.mine: Wrong, 41 only IF the first house uses 5 sticks; the prompt never says so
findings.why: My answer matches the key in substance, but only by guessing the hidden premise. The prompt gives neither the stick-house picture nor the first house's stick count; '41' cannot be derived from the words alone (a 6-stick first house would give 42). Answerable only if the lesson shows the 5-stick house immediately before this item; as a standalone/spaced-review item it is unanswerable.

hinglish.phrase: ek baar baad lagane ke liye kitne metre chahiye
hinglish.why: 'baad' is meant as baadh/baad (बाड़, fence) but reads as 'baad' (after): 'to put after once'. The sibling item pl-c4-maths-l01 and the class-5 items say 'fencing'/'boundary'; use 'fencing' or 'baadh'.

hinglish.phrase: Bike aamon ka bar 20 aur 30 ke theek beech mein rukta hai
hinglish.why: 'Bike' (बिके, sold) at sentence start reads as English 'bike'; a reader or TTS voice will say 'bike'. 'Beche gaye aamon ka bar' is unambiguous. (Same spelling mid-sentence in pl-c5-maths-e01 'tickets bike' is less confusing.)
Transliteration diacritic 'ṛ' in otherwise plain Roman Hinglish (every other item writes 'chauda'); wrong script mix for display/TTS.

level.why: Needs the average (mean) of two numbers and gives a decimal answer 12.5. Average is not in the class 5 NCERT syllabus (arithmetic mean arrives in class 7 data handling); a class-5 placement item should not hinge on it.

Correct option is 'Reflex angle' (north to south-west clockwise = 225°). Class 5 NCERT angles cover acute/right/obtuse (and straight); reflex is class 6 vocabulary. Borderline (one class up), and it also needs the 8-point compass.

other_notes: All 188 keys agree with my blind answers; no key_wrong and no acceptable_wrong found after scanning every acceptable list.

Unfilled template placeholder {friendF} appears in prompt_en, prompt_hi, options and keys of c5-maths-ch12-t01-rl-h1 and DIAG:c5-maths-ch12-t02-m-bigger-time-faster. Fine if substituted at runtime (the key's acceptable forms carry the same placeholder, so matching must substitute there too).

Placement items with format 'numeric' whose key is not a plain number: pl-c4-maths-e11 ('3/8'), pl-c5-maths-e03 ('3/4'), pl-c4-maths-m11 ('3:25 p.m.'), pl-c5-maths-l12 ('12.5'). Check the numeric input/matcher accepts fractions, a clock time with p.m., and decimals.

Near-duplicate placement items across bands (same numbers, same answer): pl-c4-maths-m05 = pl-c4-maths-l01 (18 m × 7 m garden, 50 m); pl-c5-maths-m10 = pl-c5-maths-l02 (18 × 12 garden, 60 m); pl-c5-maths-m11 = pl-c5-maths-l05 (2 min 35 s = 155 s); pl-c5-maths-m12 = pl-c5-maths-l07 (buses 12 and 18 min, 36). A child who meets both gets the same question twice, and the 'late' band is no harder than 'mid'.

Loose acceptable forms (not wrong answers, but they accept an incomplete reply): c4-maths-ch13-t01-i09 accepts bare '64' for 'what are the two parts, and the total'; c4-maths-ch03-t01-i07 accepts bare '16' for 'odd or even?'; c5-maths-ch03-t01-i10 accepts 'quarter turn' with no direction.
